reading.read_method: Full sequential first-hand text reading from the exact hash-verified private TXT member on the user's authorized Lappy; chapter boundaries and nonempty-line locators re-derived without exporting text.

evidence.observation: Sisko finds Jennifer and Jake beneath wreckage during a ship evacuation; the account distinguishes the rescue of the child from the unrecoverable adult.
Kira questions whether invited Federation assistance can coexist with meaningful Bajoran self-rule.
After his confrontation with Sisko, the narration gives Picard awareness of the name and death of Sisko's spouse, separately depicting his self-blame.
Contact with the orb brings Sisko a perceptually detailed replay of meeting Jennifer before their marriage.
O'Brien remembers a fatal confrontation during a rescue on Setlik, alongside the deaths of a colleague and a commander's family.
Dax explicitly speaks of joined existence with more than one contributing subject and pushes back on Sisko's singular-host framing.
Dax's contact with the orb presents the joining as an experience accessed through both the former host's and the new host's viewpoints.
Sisko and Dax describe incompatible immediate landscapes while standing together at a wormhole destination.
An interlocutor adopting the appearance of Sisko's son asks about time, while Sisko attempts to explain human sequential experience.
A memory-form interlocutor questions why Sisko remains in the moment of traumatic loss, despite his expressed wish to leave it.
Sisko acknowledges that his grief has held his attention in the destroyed ship, exposing conflict between physical departure and lived psychological time.
Jake and Nog cooperate in extinguishing a fire and freeing Nog's trapped father, despite earlier disagreement over property and conduct.
Odo reluctantly assists a wounded civilian at the doctor's direction; earlier antagonism becomes situational cooperation.
Sisko's perspective toward Picard changes from involuntary Borg-associated images to recognition of the injured human before him.
Opaka declines Sisko's offer to describe the wormhole beings directly and frames that refusal as a spiritual boundary.

unresolved.reason: The TXT has no verified title or imprint page; the publisher's catalog establishes a plausible novel Work but does not authenticate the private TXT manifestation.
Twelve consecutive chapters and a narrative ending were observed, but a publisher text/pagination comparison was not available.
Novel prose includes expanded flashbacks and apparent source-specific biographical assertions; audiovisual continuity and later series retroactive corrections were not reconciled.
Figures that look and speak like Sisko's loved ones inside the encounter are narrative presentation forms, not evidence that the originals are present.
No global Work or character identity decisions are authorized for this LIT worker.
